How often and from what do you develop changes to your fitness routine?

We change training every work out. When I was powerlifting we followed the Westside Barbell method that Louie Simmons, Dave Tate and others have helped develop over the years, and one of the core tenants there is "everything works, but nothing works forever" which is to say that your body will adapt to whatever stresses you place on it, so change up the exercises every couple of weeks or so before your body has a chance to get used to the exercises you are doing.

That's the basics of it, and as far as what exercises to switch around, go check out fitness channels on YouTube, and you will literally have more exercises to do for each body part than you will have time to do said exercises.

Athlean RX is a very good follow on YouTube, very smart and informative. Happy training.

How often do your fitness goals change? New goals = different routine. How often do you find your current routine to be flawed or inadequate? How often do you just decide you want to try something different, and then you wind up sticking with it?

I've been doing the same basic routine for about 8 months now and I am still seeing progress from it. The only thing I have varied are reps and the times of the day. If my fitness goals change at any point, then my routine will. I have sought advice from various people and have done my own searching online. At the end of the day, it's all about sticking to your plan. Nothing will work if you can't stick to it, so it's about finding out what you can stick to. For me, I've found that the biggest factor is being able to be flexible with my schedule. If I can't do my routine whenever I want, then it's not going to get done. As a result, I've chosen to focus on very basic exercises that don't require any special equipment.
